### Timestamp

```csharp
public TimeSpan Timestamp { get; }
```

When the event happened, on a monotonic clock, as near as the platform says: on desktop, when the system saw it; elsewhere, when the platform delivered it. Gesture recognizers measure press durations from this value so classification is immune to game-thread dispatch delays, and it's fine enough for velocities. Only differences between timestamps are meaningful.

### TouchCount

```csharp
public int TouchCount { get; }
```

The number of touches down after this event: a touch's Began counts itself, and its Ended or Canceled doesn't, so the last touch to lift reports 0. Only touches count: a mouse or pen event always reports 0, even with a button held, so on a Began, games tell touch input from mouse input by it.

### TouchIndex

```csharp
public int TouchIndex { get; }
```

Which of the touches down this one is, from 0.
